gaps: The promised out-of-scope list has no defined treatment for writable paths excluded from task measurement and review. `.factory/`, `plans/`, and `docs/decisions/` are excluded, so changes there cannot appear in a list derived only from the measured product diff. Specify how those changes are exposed and judged before shipping. (docs/specs/full-access.md:22; docs/specs/full-access.md:31; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:89; factory/scripts/factory_lib.py:4397)

The spec requires refreshing an open PR’s out-of-scope list but does not say how to preserve its existing body, including human edits and Ticket lines. The current seal path creates a PR and merely reports an existing one. (docs/specs/full-access.md:35; factory/scripts/forge_cli/tasks.py:717; factory/scripts/forge_cli/tasks.py:738)

Removing the close-time launch requirement leaves active-stage measurement amendments dependent on a recorded launch: the decomposition recorder refuses an amendment without one, and its continuity receipt requires a launch ID. Specify the launch-free continuity authority so a task can correct `write_scope`, tests, or verify commands mid-stage. (docs/specs/full-access.md:37; factory/scripts/record_decomposition_from_json.py:385; factory/scripts/record_decomposition_from_json.py:393; factory/scripts/factory_lib.py:3986)

The Lite criterion does not define whether its budget and review cover every committed change. Current Lite close filters to product files, exempts some files from the budget, and reviews a similarly filtered scope; unrestricted writes can therefore accompany a closed Lite ticket without being counted or reviewed. (docs/specs/full-access.md:38; factory/scripts/forge_cli/quickfix.py:326; factory/scripts/forge_cli/quickfix.py:435; factory/scripts/forge_cli/review.py:2013)

If an already-open degraded or quickfix window is supported after hook removal, its closure record will use the old claimed-files list. The current close commands do not measure subsequent edits, while claims are made by the write guard slated for deletion. Define how legacy closure records the actual changes. (docs/specs/full-access.md:40; factory/scripts/forge_cli/quickfix.py:223; factory/scripts/forge_cli/quickfix.py:302; factory/scripts/pre_tool_use.py:1832)

The proposed hook registration check needs a negative assertion that write tools are absent. `check_dual_runtime.py` checks coverage, while doctor permits inherited extra PreToolUse aliases; either could pass while Edit or `apply_patch` still routes to the hook. (docs/specs/full-access.md:47; factory/scripts/check_dual_runtime.py:400; factory/scripts/forge_cli/doctor.py:988)

The executor-mode statement lacks a delivery dependency or interim behavior. Decision 0085 specifies `FORGE_EXECUTOR` routing, but current `forge delegate` selects by coordinator runtime and has no executor resolver; publishing the proposed guidance first would describe a control that does not exist. (docs/specs/full-access.md:51; docs/decisions/0085-executor-modes.md:20; factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:2444)

Saying `strict-role-split.md` is superseded does not remove it from confirmed-spec consumers. It remains `status: confirmed`, and the spec registry treats every confirmed file as current for roadmap and sign-off. Define how existing roadmap references remain valid while the conflicting spec stops governing new work. (docs/specs/full-access.md:54; docs/specs/strict-role-split.md:4; factory/scripts/forge_cli/specs.py:79; factory/scripts/forge_cli/specs.py:111)

The documentation update list omits instructions that would direct users to a removed degraded start command or claim a launch is needed to close. In particular, QUALITY, degraded-mode, the factory reference, and the parity architecture retain those instructions. (docs/specs/full-access.md:58; docs/QUALITY.md:115; docs/degraded-mode.md:30; docs/architecture/dual-coordinator-parity.md:7)
contradictions: The spec says recorder consistency keeps `.factory` state trustworthy after arbitrary edits, but accepted Decision 0087 explicitly says a consistent hand-edited record is not detected and records are unsigned. State the narrower assurance without implying recorder provenance. (docs/specs/full-access.md:25; docs/decisions/0087-full-access-close-checks.md:43)

The claimed shipping boundary does not match the PR ticket check. It accepts story and quickfix records, permits harness-source and re-vendor exceptions, infers tickets from branches, and checks only minimal task-marker fields rather than task approval. The generated task PR body also contains no literal `Ticket:` line. Resolve which boundary is intended. (docs/specs/full-access.md:27; factory/scripts/check_pr_ticket.py:193; factory/scripts/check_pr_ticket.py:213; factory/scripts/check_pr_ticket.py:241; factory/scripts/check_pr_ticket.py:270; factory/scripts/forge_cli/tasks.py:716)

The promised post-upgrade closure of an already-open window conflicts with accepted Decision 0088, which requires upgrade to refuse while any worktree has a Lite window or other work in progress. Specify a reachable migration path or remove the post-upgrade case. (docs/specs/full-access.md:40; docs/decisions/0088-simple-upgrade.md:23)

The absolute criterion that a coordinator Bash write to any file is never refused by a Forge hook conflicts with the explicitly retained destructive-command denylist: for example, a Bash `rm -rf` write is refused. Qualify the criterion by the retained command-policy gates. (docs/specs/full-access.md:64; docs/specs/full-access.md:81; factory/scripts/pre_tool_use.py:1338)
resolutions: The review brief uses the full task diff since the stage base and lists changed records, plans and decisions separately, so paths excluded from product measurement are still shown to the reviewer (Behaviour: Task close; AC3).
The PR body keeps a Forge-owned marked block; re-running close replaces only that block (appends if absent) and never touches human edits or Ticket lines (Behaviour: Task close; AC4).
Mid-stage amendments of write scope, tests or verify commands bind to the active stage instead of a recorded launch (Behaviour: Scope corrections mid-task; AC5).
Lite mode done reviews every committed change since the window opened and counts every non-test, non-Markdown file (previous exemptions dropped) against the budget (Behaviour: Lite; AC6).

Degraded and quickfix windows are removed entirely (start and close); no window may be open here at merge, and clients cannot carry one across because upgrade refuses open windows; old closed records stay valid history (Behaviour: Removed; AC7).
check_dual_runtime.py and doctor now also assert that Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit/apply_patch are NOT routed to the hook (Behaviour: Hooks kept; AC8).
No executor guidance is added here; forge delegate keeps handing work to Codex, and the executor setting stays with the warm-threads story (Behaviour: Who writes).
strict-role-split.md is marked superseded: it stops being offered for new roadmap links while existing links still resolve (Behaviour: Canon; AC9).
The docs list now includes docs/QUALITY.md, docs/FACTORY.md and the parity architecture, and docs/degraded-mode.md is deleted (Behaviour: Canon).
The assurance is stated narrowly: recorders check consistency; a deliberate consistent hand edit is not detected because records are unsigned, matching decision 0087 (Behaviour: Writing).

The shipping boundary is the existing PR ticket check exactly (closed task marker, closed Lite window or re-vendor, via a Ticket: line or the canonical branch); task markers exist only after an approved, proven, reviewed close (Behaviour: Shipping; AC2).
The post-upgrade open-window case is removed: close commands go too, and upgrade refuses open windows (Behaviour: Removed).
The criterion is qualified: never refused because of the file written; the retained command gates still refuse destructive commands, raw codex exec and unsigned phase advances (AC1).

artifact_delta.cold:
- Any agent may edit any file at any time. No hook refuses or claims a write
  because of what it writes or where: product and canon files, `.factory/`
  records, conflicted files, other worktrees and paths under symlinked
  parents are all writable. Recorded state stays trustworthy through the
  recorders' consistency checks, as today.
- The boundary moves from writing to shipping. Unplanned work can be written
  but cannot ship: every PR still needs a `Ticket:` naming an approved task or
  a closed Lite window (the PR ticket check), and a task closes only with an
  approved plan, passing proof and a clean review.
- `task close` keeps its proof, review and seal. The review brief lists every
  file in the task's measured diff that is outside its declared write scope,
  derived from the diff itself (not only from recorded scope amendments), and
  names any that overlap the write scope of another active task in the story.
  The task PR body carries the same list; when close runs again on an already
  open PR, it refreshes that list in the PR body. Nothing here refuses.
- Close no longer requires a recorded Codex launch or a degraded window.
- Lite windows stay: `mode done` measures the committed diff since the window
  opened and still enforces the file budget and clean reviews.
- Degraded mode and the old quickfix window can no longer be started;
  starting either prints a one-line explanation and changes nothing. A window
  already open from before the upgrade can still be closed or abandoned with
  its existing command, so no task is stuck behind it.
- Still enforced by hooks: the question gate, the ban on raw `codex exec` and
  direct companion launches, the commit check, the sign-off gate and the
  destructive-command denylist. The hook registration contract becomes:
  Claude's PreToolUse matcher covers `Bash` and `AskUserQuestion`; Codex's
  covers its shell tool and `request_user_input`. Edit, Write, MultiEdit,
  NotebookEdit and `apply_patch` are no longer routed to the hook, and
  `check_dual_runtime.py` and `forge doctor` check this contract.
- The executor mode (decision 0085) says who is expected to write and whom
  `forge delegate` hands work to; it is not a write lock. Decision 0087 amends
  0085 accordingly.
- `docs/specs/strict-role-split.md` is superseded by this spec. The criteria
  in `delegation-boundary.md` and `dual-coordinator-parity.md` that require
  out-of-scope refusal, coordinator write denial, protected-state write
  enforcement or a degraded substitute are replaced by this spec's criteria.
- The session-start message, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, WORKFLOW.md, the Forge
  skill, the product brief and `workflow-modes.md` describe the new rule in
  one or two sentences.
artifact_delta.final:
**Writing.** No hook refuses or claims a write because of the file it writes
or where it is: product and canon files, `.factory/` records, conflicted
files, other worktrees and paths under symlinked parents are all writable.
The retained command gates still apply to the commands themselves (below).
Recorders keep checking records for consistency; a deliberate, consistent
hand edit of a record is not detected because records are not signed, as
today.

**Shipping.** The boundary is the existing PR ticket check, unchanged: every
PR declares a completed work record (a closed task marker, a closed Lite
window, or a harness re-vendor) through a `Ticket:` line or its canonical
branch name. A task marker exists only after `task close`, which needs an
approved plan, passing proof and a clean review. Unplanned work can be
written but cannot ship without such a record.

**Task close.** `task close` keeps its proof, review and seal, and no longer
requires a recorded Codex launch. The review brief lists every file in the
task's full diff since its stage base that is outside the declared write
scope, derived from the diff itself (not from scope amendments), names any
that overlap another active task's write scope, and lists changed records,
plans and decisions separately so the reviewer sees them too. The task PR
body carries the same list inside a Forge-owned marked block; re-running
close on an open PR replaces only that block (appending it if absent) and
never touches the rest of the body. Nothing here refuses.

**Scope corrections mid-task.** Amending a task's write scope, tests or verify
commands during an active stage no longer needs a recorded launch; the
recorder binds the amendment to the active stage instead.

**Lite.** `mode done` reviews every committed change since the window opened
(nothing filtered out) and counts every committed file except tests and
Markdown against the five-file budget, including files previously exempt.

**Removed.** Degraded mode and the old quickfix window are removed entirely:
their start and close commands say they were removed and change nothing.
Existing closed records stay readable and still satisfy the ticket check for
history. No window may be open in this repository when this change merges;
client repos can't carry one across, because upgrade refuses open windows.

**Hooks kept.** The question gate, the ban on raw `codex exec` and direct
companion launches, the commit check, the sign-off gate and the
destructive-command denylist. Registration contract: Claude's PreToolUse
matcher covers `Bash` and `AskUserQuestion`; Codex's covers its shell tool and
`request_user_input`; Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit and `apply_patch`
must NOT be routed to the hook. `check_dual_runtime.py` and `forge doctor`
check both what is covered and what is absent.

**Who writes.** `forge delegate` keeps handing work to Codex as today. The
executor setting planned in the warm-threads story will choose whom delegate
hands work to; this story adds no executor guidance.

**Canon.** `docs/specs/strict-role-split.md` is marked superseded by this
spec: it stops governing new work, and roadmap items already linked to it
stay valid. The criteria in `delegation-boundary.md` and
`dual-coordinator-parity.md` that require out-of-scope refusal, coordinator
write denial, protected-state write enforcement or a degraded substitute are
replaced by this spec's criteria. `docs/degraded-mode.md` is deleted. The
session-start message, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, WORKFLOW.md, the Forge skill,
the product brief, `workflow-modes.md`, `docs/QUALITY.md`, `docs/FACTORY.md`
and the parity architecture describe the new rule in one or two sentences
and stop mentioning degraded mode or a launch requirement.
